items.text: ECB deposit rate stands at 2.50% as of Nov 16, 2026, with OIS pricing implying 93% chance of a 25bp hike at the Dec 17 meeting. WTI down 0.09 to 89.53 and Brent up 0.80 to 92.94; near-flat on the week but oil remains elevated, pressuring refining margins and amplifying spreads on energy credits—watch for potential debt stress if prices retest recent lows.

October payrolls printed +165K (a +105K surprise from prior 60K); unemployment edged down to 4.1%. Initial claims flat at 203K. Surface strength masks composition risk: ADP payrolls showed only 86K in Oct, skewing services; manufacturing jobs softening. For credit, this is late-cycle labor support but with deteriorating breadth—watch for capex/M&A pullbacks if breadth truly breaks.

Year-ahead inflation expectations decreased from 4.7% to 3.7% from October (Nov survey); headline CPI at 3.72% YoY (Sep), core at 2.57%. PPI surged to 6.52% YoY (Oct, +0.23pts), driven by oil. Services inflation (ISM Prices 73) remains hot and sticky; core PCE likely still 3%+. Headline CPI volatility remains a tail risk for Fed taper/pivot scenarios that could shock credit valuations.

Fed funds frozen at 4.00%; 2-10 curve steepened to 28bps from 27bps; 10Y yields compressed 18bps to 4.92% and 2Y down 17bps to 4.63%. ECB on brink of potential tightening (25bp hike odds 93% for Dec 17). Rate markets pricing mild Fed cuts in 2027 but ECB inversion risk rising. For credit: front-end relief (tighter HY OAS 3.63 from 3.47) masks duration convexity risk and CCC distress widening to 13.87 from 13.53—bifurcation accelerating.

HY OAS tightened to 3.63bps from 3.47 on rate relief; IG OAS widened marginally to 97bps from 93bps. CCC OAS blew out to 13.87 from 13.53—a 34bp move in one day. The divergence between IG/HY and CCC is a red flag: covenant-lite/low-quality credits are repricing default risk. Stress is real; look for fallen angels and loan defaults clustering in 2027 as refinancing peaks.

China NBS Manufacturing PMI decreased to 49.30 points in October from 50.10 points in September of 2026; small and mid-cap firms contracted (PMI 47.5–48.4). US GDP nowcast holding 3.21% (Oct 1 vintage); Q3 actual was 3.4%. For 2026 through October, Retail Sales growth has been strong, averaging +0.6% monthly versus the long-term average of +0.4%. US growth holding up, but China weakness and profit warnings from cap-intensive sectors raise medium-term risk; credit spreads not fully pricing export/demand slowdown tail.

The University of Michigan's Consumer Sentiment Index rose 7.3% to 51.5 in November, up from 48.0 in October, helped by post-election optimism and lower gas prices—but sentiment remains in 1st percentile historically. Current Economic Conditions registered at 49.4, up from 46.7 in October. Housing starts improved to 1309K from 1191K; existing home sales fell to 3.75M from 3.97M (lagged Oct data). Consumer holding up on goods spending but sentiment still fragile; housing breadth poor despite start pick-up—watch for mortgage stress (7.28% rates) and construction credit deterioration.

themeCards.title: CCC Distress & Leverage Repricing
themeCards.statusLine: CCC OAS blew out to 13.87 from 13.53 in a single day; covenant-lite/low-quality credit repricing accelerating. IG/HY holding but CCC blowout signals default risk concentration in lower credit quality.
themeCards.relevance: For special situations: This is the breeding ground for distressed opportunities. Rising CCC spreads with relatively benign macro backdrop suggest over-tightening in Oct-Nov has reversed, exposing overleveraged mid-cap and lower-quality names. Restructuring/covenant waivers likely; selective deep-value entry now possible if spreads stabilize.

themeCards.title: China Demand & Refinancing Wall Risk
themeCards.statusLine: China's manufacturing activity returns to contraction in October after a brief improvement, with its purchasing managers' index falling to 49.3 and new export orders weakening. EMs and commodity credits vulnerable.
themeCards.relevance: China PMI below 50 and export orders collapsing signal demand shock. High-yield energy and materials credits, plus emerging-market corporate bonds (esp. China-linked), face refinancing headwinds in H1 2027. Watch for covenant pressure in commodity-linked credit lines and cross-border funding stress.

themeCards.title: ECB Tightening into US Rate Stability
themeCards.statusLine: OIS pricing implies a 93% chance of a 25bp hike at that meeting (Dec 17 ECB decision); Fed holding at 4.0%. EUR carry unwind risk rising, widening EUR-USD spreads.
themeCards.relevance: ECB hikes while Fed pauses creates relative rate divergence and cross-currency basis risk. Hedging costs for USD issuers with EUR liabilities rise; euro-denominated corporate credit (esp. financials) faces carry pressure. Potential flight from EUR risk assets into USD credits—watch for intra-European credit dislocation.

themeCards.title: Mortgage Rate Stress & Housing Credit Linkages
themeCards.statusLine: Current Economic Conditions registered at 49.4, up from 46.7 in October; existing home sales fell to 3.75M from 3.97M. Mortgage rates at 7.28% are sustained pressure on affordability.
themeCards.relevance: Existing home sales falling despite rising sentiment signals affordability wall. RMBS/CMBS servicers and REITs under pressure; potential for loan modifications and default wave in 2027. Special situations: distressed REIT debt, non-agency RMBS with payment shock, and construction credit linkages to home builder covenant waivers.

themeCards.title: Labor Breadth Deterioration & Capex Uncertainty
themeCards.statusLine: ADP payrolls (86K) lag official (165K); ISM Services Employment only at 51.4; manufacturing sector softening. October print likely inflated by prior-month reversal; true momentum weaker.
themeCards.relevance: Divergence between headline and composition suggests late-cycle labor fatigue. Capex guidance reductions and M&A deal volume likely to contract, hitting financial services, consulting, and cyclical services revenues. Special situations: watch for covenant-flex deals, pre-bankruptcy restructuring activity in lower-rated lev finance portfolios, and capex/dividend cuts.

regime.label: Late-cycle bifurcation
regime.detail: Fed on hold, macro resilient but labor/breadth fading, CCC spreads widening, China weakening, ECB tightening into USD strength—credit quality divergence accelerating; IG holding spreads but lower-rated leverage repricing default risk.
